content.title: Polynomial Zeros, Multiplicity, and End Behavior
content.overview: This lesson focuses on analyzing the behavior of polynomial functions based on their factored forms. By identifying zeros, their multiplicities, and the leading coefficient, you can predict how a graph behaves at specific x-intercepts and as it extends toward infinity.
learning_objectives: Identify zeros and their multiplicities from a factored polynomial.
Determine if a graph crosses or touches the x-axis at a specific zero based on multiplicity.
Calculate the degree of a polynomial by summing multiplicities.
Predict the end behavior of a polynomial using its degree and leading coefficient.

sections.title: Zeros and Multiplicity
sections.content: A zero (or root) of a polynomial is an x-value that makes the function equal to zero. In a factored polynomial like f(x) = a(x - r)^m, the value 'r' is the zero. The exponent 'm' is the multiplicity of that zero. Multiplicity tells us how many times a specific factor is repeated in the polynomial. For example, in f(x) = (x - 5)^2, the zero is 5 and its multiplicity is 2.

sections.title: Local Behavior at the x-axis
sections.content: The multiplicity of a zero determines the graph's behavior at that x-intercept. If the multiplicity is odd (1, 3, 5...), the graph crosses the x-axis and changes sign. If the multiplicity is even (2, 4, 6...), the graph touches the x-axis and rebounds (turns around), staying on the same side of the axis.

sections.title: Degree and End Behavior
sections.content:
The degree of a polynomial is the sum of all multiplicities of its factors. End behavior describes what happens to f(x) as x approaches positive or negative infinity. If the degree is even, both ends of the graph point in the same direction. If the degree is odd, the ends point in opposite directions. The leading coefficient (the constant 'a' in front) determines the specific direction: a positive leading coefficient means the right side (as x → ∞) always rises.

![A flowchart showing the steps to analyze a polynomial: Identify Factors, Determine Multiplicities, Sum for Degree, Check Leading Coefficient, and Predict Behavior.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/09874d99-b098-4a53-8d6d-e1b0140fdf1b-1786505719773-299.webp)

worked_examples.question: Given f(x) = -2(x + 4)^2(x - 3)^3, describe the behavior at x = -4 and the end behavior of the graph.
worked_examples.solution: 1. Identify the zero and multiplicity: For the factor (x + 4)^2, the zero is x = -4 and the multiplicity is 2. 2. Determine local behavior: Since the multiplicity (2) is even, the graph touches the x-axis at x = -4 and rebounds. 3. Calculate degree: Sum the exponents (2 + 3 = 5). The degree is 5 (odd). 4. Identify leading coefficient: The leading coefficient is -2 (negative). 5. Determine end behavior: For an odd degree with a negative leading coefficient, the graph rises to the left (f(x) → ∞ as x → -∞) and falls to the right (f(x) → -∞ as x → ∞).

common_mistakes: Confusing the sign of the zero: In (x + 3), the zero is -3, not 3.
Forgetting that a factor like (x) has a multiplicity of 1 and a zero of 0.
Assuming all even-degree polynomials have both ends pointing up; they only point up if the leading coefficient is positive.
exam_tips: Quick Check: If the degree is even, the ends match (both up or both down). If the degree is odd, they differ.
The right-hand end behavior (as x → ∞) always matches the sign of the leading coefficient.
Sum the exponents of all factors to find the degree quickly.
content.recap: To analyze a polynomial, identify zeros and multiplicities from factors. Odd multiplicity crosses the x-axis; even multiplicity touches and turns. The sum of multiplicities is the degree, which, combined with the leading coefficient, dictates the end behavior.

knowledge_claims.content: A zero of a polynomial is an x-value that results in a function value of zero, represented by 'r' in the factor (x - r).
Multiplicity is the exponent 'm' associated with a factor (x - r)^m in a polynomial's factored form.
If a zero has an odd multiplicity, the graph of the polynomial crosses the x-axis at that zero.
If a zero has an even multiplicity, the graph of the polynomial touches the x-axis and rebounds at that zero.
The degree of a factored polynomial is calculated by summing the multiplicities (exponents) of all its linear factors.
Even-degree polynomials have ends that point in the same direction, while odd-degree polynomials have ends that point in opposite directions.
A positive leading coefficient indicates that as x approaches positive infinity, the function f(x) also approaches positive infinity.
A negative leading coefficient indicates that as x approaches positive infinity, the function f(x) approaches negative infinity.
It is a mistake to assume the zero of (x + k) is k; the zero is actually -k.
A factor written as 'x' without a visible exponent has a zero of 0 and a multiplicity of 1.
To verify end behavior for an even-degree polynomial with a negative leading coefficient, ensure both ends approach negative infinity.
The total number of x-intercepts (including those where the graph touches) cannot exceed the degree of the polynomial.

videoLesson.title: Determine Zero Multiplicity and End Behavior
videoLesson.description: Recognize each zero and its multiplicity from the polynomial's factors and leading coefficient. Use multiplicity to decide crossing versus touching and degree plus leading coefficient to predict end behavior.
